definition: Extending software CI/CD with data and model gates: every change to prompts, models, or retrieval triggers the eval suite, and regressions block deployment.
details: Extending software CI/CD with data and model gates: every change to prompts, models, or retrieval triggers the eval suite, and regressions block deployment. For LLM products, the eval-in-CI loop replaces the unit-test safety net that nondeterministic outputs break.

explainer.lead: CD for ML adds data and model checks to continuous delivery. Every change to a prompt, model, or retrieval setup must pass an evaluation suite before release, so a regression stops deployment instead of reaching users.

tiers.eli5: Imagine checking a robot's answers every time you change its instructions, brain, or way of finding information. If its answers get worse, it is not allowed to start work. This is like a final school test that must be passed before each new version can be used.
tiers.practitioner: Run the evaluation suite in CI whenever prompts, models, or retrieval configuration change, and gate deployment on regression checks. Treat evaluations as the release safety net for LLM products: nondeterministic outputs mean conventional unit tests alone cannot provide the same protection.
tiers.paperLevel: Let c be a change to prompts, model, or retrieval, and let E(c) be the evaluation-suite results: deployment proceeds only when the configured gates detect no regression. This extends CI/CD with data and model gates, replacing the unit-test-only safety net that nondeterministic LLM outputs undermine.

explainer.example: A team edits a customer-support assistant's prompt and updates its retrieval setup. The change triggers the evaluation suite, which finds a regression, so the deployment gate blocks the release rather than shipping the worse assistant.

usedIn.name: LLM product deployment
usedIn.detail: Prompt and model updates must pass evaluations before release.

usedIn.name: Retrieval-based AI systems
usedIn.detail: Retrieval changes trigger the evaluation suite so regressions can block deployment.

usedIn.name: MLOps delivery pipelines
usedIn.detail: Data and model gates extend conventional software CI/CD.

explainer.intuition: Software delivery already checks that changes do not break the system; CD for ML applies the same release discipline to model behavior. The evaluation suite becomes the gate between an LLM change and its users.
howItWorks: A prompt, model, or retrieval setup changes.
The change automatically triggers the evaluation suite.
Deployment gates check the results for regressions.
A passing change proceeds; a regression blocks deployment.
explainer.whyItMatters: It prevents prompt, model, and retrieval regressions from automatically reaching production. For LLM products, it supplies a release safety net where nondeterministic outputs weaken the protection offered by unit tests.
misconceptions: It is not ordinary CI/CD with no extra gates: data and model evaluations are part of delivery.
It is not a claim that LLM outputs are deterministic unit tests.
A triggered evaluation does not guarantee deployment; regressions block it.

diagram.caption: Every relevant change flows through evaluation and a regression gate before deployment.
